verdicts.reason: A: book and headline work, but the bottom row crams a tiny CTA pill, a logo too small to read, the eyebrow and the legal text into one line, so the CTA is buried and the logo is barely visible. B: the eyebrow is enlarged until it competes with the headline, and it sits below the body copy. The CTA, the tiny unreadable logo and the wrapped fine print are pushed into a cramped cluster at the far right, away from the message. Both are weak; A's single row holds together slightly better.

A: tiny buried CTA and a logo too small to read, crammed into one bottom row with the eyebrow and the legal text. B: a large, clear CTA in its own right column gives proper hierarchy, and the book and headline read well. Its flaws are the oversized eyebrow placed below the body copy, a still-tiny logo, and the fine print jammed next to it.

A: drops the book cover, the original's key image, and nearly all the confetti. It leaves a large dead area in the middle right, a lone floating line of legal text, and a tiny CTA, a stray book thumbnail and an unreadable logo crammed into the bottom-right corner. B keeps the book, the confetti and a clear headline, though its CTA and logo are too small and squeezed into the bottom row.
